tier: Styx supported public contract; upstream Cua catalog remains separately pinned; no native acceptance claim
instructions: Use browser_* for webpage and tab automation, Exec for CLI/process work, and computer tools for native desktop applications or browser chrome. The agent chooses the tool; failed calls never trigger local automatic fallback. Browser element targets belong to this chat and current observation: use browser_snapshot without filename to get fresh targets after navigation, tab changes or reconnection. Default to exec_command for Git/GitHub clone, downloads (curl/wget), file operations, builds, tests and other CLI/development work. Interactive foreground or TTY sessions managed by exec_command/write_stdin are Exec sessions. Do not open Terminal or another desktop terminal through Spotlight, launchers or computer tools to paste these commands. If Exec fails, is disconnected, or reports authentication, permission or sandbox errors, check get_execution_environment_status, resolve the specific Exec issue or report the blocker; never use a desktop terminal to bypass it. Styx v1 window observations use two separate reads with the observed pid and window_id: get_window_state(include_screenshot:false) for the complete element tree and fresh element_token values, and get_window_state(include_accessibility_tree:false) for a screenshot. Omit full_output, capture_mode, since, query and file-output options. For set_value, also send the observed pid and window_id with the fresh element_token and value; the v1 exact-target write requires all four fields. A screenshot alone does not authorize input; use a fresh element_token for the supported element action. Combined tree-and-screenshot acquisition is not supported in this release; its refusal is not evidence that the user needs another OS permission. For native desktop tasks, discover apps/windows and observe with the advertised read tools, then use a fresh element_token for click or exact set_value. Keyboard typing, key presses, scrolling and pixel input have no admitted Host target route in this release and are not advertised. Do not infer complete upstream SDK support from the installed worker. Use the app bundle identifier or observed PID when localized app names do not match. An explicitly requested GUI workflow may use computer tools; this does not authorize bypassing an Exec restriction. Do not replace desktop tools with osascript, AppleScript/System Events, JXA or shell-driven input automation, including when a computer tool fails. Those paths have separate macOS permissions and can expose a node authorization prompt. For computer_snapshot_required or stale element references, observe again and use the new references; never reuse another conversation's references. For a permission or connection error, check get_execution_environment_status and report the specific missing permission or connection. Do not reset permissions or request additional Node/System Events access as a desktop fallback. Only use application scripting when the user explicitly requests that scripting workflow, explain its separate Automation permission before the first invocation, and let the user grant it through macOS. Styx desktop permission does not authorize that separate path.

tools.name: exec_command
tools.description: Run a command; return output or an owned interactive session. Default to exec_command for Git/GitHub clone, downloads (curl/wget), file operations, builds, tests and other CLI/development work. Interactive foreground or TTY sessions managed by exec_command/write_stdin are Exec sessions. Do not open Terminal or another desktop terminal through Spotlight, launchers or computer tools to paste these commands. If Exec fails, is disconnected, or reports authentication, permission or sandbox errors, check get_execution_environment_status, resolve the specific Exec issue or report the blocker; never use a desktop terminal to bypass it. For native GUI reading or interaction use Styx computer tools, not osascript/System Events or shell-driven input. Do not fall back to scripting after a desktop error; refresh stale observations or report the missing permission. Explicit user-requested application scripting needs separate macOS Automation consent.

tools.name: browser_find
tools.description: Search the accessibility snapshot of the current page for text or a regular expression. Returns matching snapshot nodes with a few lines of surrounding context (like search snippets), each shown under its path from the root of the tree, which is cheaper than capturing the whole snapshot when you only need to locate an element and its ref.

text.description: Plain text to search for in the page snapshot (case-insensitive substring match). Provide either text or regex, not both.

regex.description: Regular expression to search for in the page snapshot. Matching is case-sensitive by default; wrap the pattern in slashes to add flags, e.g. "/error/i" for case-insensitive. Provide either text or regex, not both.

filename.description: Save results to a file instead of returning them in the response. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root.

expect.description: One to eight predicates, combined with logical AND.

exists.description:
Assert that at least one trusted element matches the selector.

Element walks are not yet exhaustive on every platform, so absence
cannot be proven. `false` is rejected instead of returning an
indefinitely-unknown predicate.

include_screenshot.description:
Return the final window screenshot as image content for a multimodal
caller. The driver does not interpret that image.

stable_samples.description: Consecutive satisfied samples required before returning success.

timeout_ms.description: Bounded wait. Zero performs one sample.
